hints: Look carefully at the x-axis first. The reaction goes left to right, so the flat line on the left must be reactants and the flat line on the right must be products. Which graphs get this the right way round?
Remember activation energy is always measured upwards from the reactants energy level to the top of the curve, and an enzyme must give a lower top without changing the start and end levels.
walkthrough:
**Read the axes correctly**

Think of the graph like a story from left to right. The left flat part is where you start, so that must be reactants. The right flat part is where you finish, so that must be products.

Quickly check all four graphs and cross out any where the labels are back to front.

**Recall what an enzyme does**

An enzyme does not add energy or change the products. It simply provides an alternative route with a lower hump.

So you expect: same start level, same end level, but the dashed enzyme curve peaks lower than the solid no enzyme curve.

**Check the activation energy arrow**

Activation energy ($E_a$) is the push needed to get started:
$$E_a = \text{energy of peak} - \text{energy of reactants}$$
So the arrow must start at the reactants level and go up to the top of the enzyme curve. Only D shows all three ideas correctly: reactants on the left, products lower on the right for an exothermic reaction, lower enzyme peak, and the arrow drawn from reactants.

options.A: The labels are reversed. The left start is labelled products and the right finish is labelled reactants, which is back to front.
options.B: The activation energy arrow is drawn from the products level, not the reactants level, so it does not show true activation energy.
options.C: The labels are reversed again. The reaction starts at the products level on the left and ends at the reactants level on the right.
options.D: Reactants start on the left, products finish lower on the right, the enzyme curve is lower, and the arrow correctly shows activation energy from reactants to the enzyme peak.
